newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies narrowly mixed, marks hover at lows.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies narrowly mixed, marks hover at lows.

text.p: IMM currency futures were trading near unchanged levels early, with marks retaining a weak tone after setting another contract low overnight.
September marks slumped to a low of $0.5698 in overnight activity as the dollar continued to strengthen against the spot currency, rising to a new 41-month of 1.7635.

Many analysts see the dollar remaining on its upward path versus the mark in the intermediate term against a backdrop of strong U.S. economic fundamentals and prospects for a broadly inclusive European monetary union.
September marks declined to a new low of $0.5690 in early pit trade.

Marc Chandler, currency strategist with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said the dollar remains well-bid after testing support at 1.7580 overight and identified the Feb. 11, 1994 high of 1.7670 as its next upside objective.

He said he expected the dollar to rise above 1.8000 marks longer term but noted that short-term speculators were currently dominating the market, with recent gains fueled by those who attempted to pick a top and were subsequently forced to buy back dollars when the market moved against them.

However, Swiss franc and yen futures were keeping losses to a minimum in the early action, with September Swiss francs holding above last week's low of $0.6848 and the contract low of $0.6835 set in March.

Yen futures traded on both sides of steady after Japan's May current account surplus posted a widely anticipated sharp increase. The figure was up 154.9 percent year-on-year, but the news was expected and its impact on dollar/yen muted.
September yen has skirted support at the previous day's low of $0.008903, IMM traders said.
British pound futures were lower in a technical pullback after reaching a six-month high of $1.6910 on Tuesday, traders said.

The Bank of England's policy committee meets through Thursday, when it is expected to announce an interest rate increase of at least 25 basis points, with some analysts forecasting a 50-basis-point rise. Official British interest rates now stand at 6.5 percent.
A brokerage firm bought three-month IMM pound straddles, likely anticipating higher volatility, said a floor trader, who noted sterling vols have risen over the past few sessions.

September yen was down $0.000001 at $0.008952, marks down $0.0008 at $0.5700, Swiss francs down $0.0001 at $0.6878, sterling down $0.0050 at $1.6804, Canadian dollars up $0.0008 at $0.7312, Australian dollars down $0.0028 at $0.7444 and Mexican pesos up $0.000025 at $0.123300. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
